t: The Vikings established a fortified base at Dublin in 841, and the town grew into a commercial centre that stayed largely under Viking control until the Norman invasion launched from Wales in 1169.
Dublin Castle, founded in 1204, made the city the centre of Anglo-Norman and then English power in Ireland, and in the 18th century the city was rebuilt with wide Georgian streets and squares.

The Act of Union of 1800 ended the Parliament of Ireland in Dublin, and after the Easter Rising of 1916, the War of Independence and the Civil War the city became the capital of the Irish Free State in 1922.
dyk: Dublin's name comes from the Irish Duiblinn, "black pool", a dark tidal pool where the River Poddle entered the Liffey, on the site of the castle gardens at the rear of Dublin Castle.
ev: The Vikings establish a fortified base at Dublin
The Irish High King Brian Boru defeats the Norse at the Battle of Clontarf
King John orders the founding of Dublin Castle
The Act of Union ends the Parliament of Ireland, and Dublin loses its political status as a capital
The Easter Rising takes place in the city centre
Dublin becomes the capital of the Irish Free State

f.founded: A Viking settlement of about 841 called Dyflin, beside a Christian ecclesiastical settlement known as Duibhlinn; a Gaelic settlement, Áth Cliath, stood further up the river. The Irish government recognised 988 as the year of the city's settlement.
f.where: On Dublin Bay at the mouth of the River Liffey in the province of Leinster, on the east coast of Ireland, with the Dublin Mountains to the south.
f.known: The Viking town of Dyflin; Dublin Castle, founded in 1204; Trinity College, founded in 1592; Georgian Dublin and the Wide Streets Commission; the Parliament of Ireland until 1800; the Easter Rising of 1916; the Guinness brewery; the capital of the Irish Free State
f.today: Dublin is the capital and largest city of Ireland and the seat of its parliament, the Oireachtas.
